title: Prove exact tariffs for consecutive queries sharing a detour
body:
## Summary

Scoped mathematical proof with finite corroboration. Consecutive paid queries partition a geodesic target and all share the same replacement path. For every nondecreasing concave tariff phi with phi(0)=0, the exact best signed gain over every ambient chart and finite path length is

```text
s_i = q_1 + ... + q_i,  t = s_k,  k >= 2
M = min_{1 <= j < k} sum_{i=1}^{k-1} phi(|s_i-s_j|)
G_max = sum_i phi(q_i) - phi(t) - 2 M
```

An existing internal endpoint attains the optimum. Every common interior edge has one target credit and k paid debits, leaving coefficient -(k-1). An interval projection and piecewise concavity prove the endpoint minimum in any metric or pseudometric space. At k>=3, positive integer q_i, total rank t<=9 and phi(r)=r^(1-C), 0<C<=.01, every path has gain strictly below -9/5 in unnormalized rank-one tariff units.

This answers the consecutive-partition case of Ali Romman's #5779 Open next question 2. The single-query predecessor is cited, not audited or replayed. No new kappa, physical supplier or selected-frontier change is claimed.

## Evidence

Before: #5779 explicitly leaves several original queries outside its one-query bound. After: the new written proof gives the exact multi-query invoice and an attaining endpoint; the finite checker compares literal invoices to the cancellation formula.

Local CPython 3.12.15, standard library only:

- 126,114 candidate one-point vectors enumerate exactly 1,098 bounded metric extensions, with 79,071 hinge median checks.
- 172,470 literal path/tariff comparisons cover all one-/two-cut paths on 135 three-qubit Lagrangian charts for profiles (1,2), (2,1), (1,1,1), and one-/two-/three-cut paths on 15 two-qubit charts for (1,1). All 24 enumerated maxima and constant-endpoint attainments pass.
- 466 positive integer compositions with at least three queries and total rank at most nine pass the unit-penalty checks. The exact inequality 44^100 < 9^99*5^100 certifies the uniform power threshold. The larger-rank positive example 5-sqrt(19) lies strictly between 641101056459/10^12 and 641101056460/10^12.
- Nine hypothesis/accounting controls pass. An additional optimized invalid-CLI control rejects before emitting a receipt.
- Warning-strict normal and isolated optimized direct results agree exactly, including package-file hashes. Each registered command was timed separately at 0.65 and 0.66 seconds locally; both are under the 120-second manifest limit. The complete registered run passes.
- Committed bytes/modes and source-history preflight pass at bd2a7f38620ee3f1e706b3702a6950d2063e1e92. Official export integrity and normal/optimized read-only Git-free replays pass, with all six exported files, including the export manifest, unchanged.

From the worktree root:

```sh

```

A reviewer can replace the absolute interpreter with a local CPython 3.12 path. The direct verifier emits a generated JSON receipt with enumerated counts and SHA256 hashes of all five package files; it writes nothing. README.md specifies every finite domain and separates the finite corroboration from the universal proof.

## Limitations

The exact contract requires consecutive queries covering the whole geodesic target, all sharing the same replacement path, with every repeated paid edge charged. A nongeodesic star and a convex-tariff line example demonstrate why broader median claims fail. The rank-nine obstruction is scoped to the stated positive integer ranks and power range; larger ranks can profit.

The proof does not establish physical independent inputs, shared correction feasibility, dirty restoration, native execution/phases, retention, stock/precision, tape movement, all-size compilation or outer admission. No supplier replay or proof-kernel check was run. The selected five assumptions remain. There is no global literature-priority claim for interval geometry or concave minimization.

## Open next questions

1. Can nonconsecutive query intervals with gaps or overlaps profit from a common path? Start from their complete signed boundary multiplicities.
2. Can a physically legal shared graph realize independent target credits with a favorable complete invoice? Supply arbitrary-input maps and restoration before pricing its actual edges.

## Related open work

- #5779 proves the one-target/one-query endpoint and path bounds and poses the several-query question; this contribution changes to a consecutive query partition and retains every repeated paid edge.
- #5772 optimizes one canonical chart for a fixed P104 scalar block. This theorem instead optimizes a shared replacement path for several geodesic queries and does not replay that block.
- #5803 develops shared-query algebras, asynchronous hubs and changed physical contracts. The present result concerns only its separately declared consecutive-query tariff relaxation and makes no source-instantiation claim.
- #5881 constructs a many-channel immutable-payload counterexample for monotone tariffs. Its channel-combination model differs from the consecutive geodesic common-path invoice here; no common numerical quantity is compared.

Before DONE, this account's ten open PRs created since the advance CLAIM at 2026-10-27T10:40:16Z were refreshed. Apart from this PR and #5881 already described above, the remaining eight are:

- #5876 excludes a five-source one-triple connector class; its prefix-mask source-leaf floor differs from the present geodesic query invoice.
- #5877 proves additive call counts for two anticommuting query types; its fixed-type algebraic alphabet differs from the shared rank-metric path contract.
- #5878 bounds partial query acquisition from a full-span basis; acquisition costs differ from replacement path costs here.
- #5879 proves a binary-affine call floor with clean erasure; its rectangular free-map model differs from this fixed chart-path invoice.
- #5880 proves clean storage requirements for reversible Gaussian overwrite; storage capacity is not the tariff optimized here.
- #5882 proves tensor composition laws for dyadic helper capacity; its prime-rank capacity differs from the geodesic distance objective.
- #5883 improves an odd-axis Clifford tensor Gram bound; its spectral constant differs from the present path-tariff maximum.
- #5885 constructs maximum binary decoder splits and equal-valued cuts; its supplied-block extraction problem differs from the consecutive-query detour problem.

None supplies a common computed numerical quantity requiring agreement or disagreement with this result. No extra mathematical computations were run to check those contributions.
